name: Sensor

claims.claim_text: A transducer is the piece of instantiated physics that converts a physical quantity such as strain, temperature or a particle flux into an electrical signal; a sensor contains a transducer but usually adds linearisation, computation and interface circuitry around it.
claims.quote_verbatim: a transducer is the little piece of, uh, of, of kind of instantiated physics that turns something like a strain or a temperature

claims.claim_text: Transducing a real-world activity into an electrical signal is the first stage of any measurement system, and what matters thereafter is the signal itself, which persists through conversion to digital, compression and transport without ceasing to be the thing of interest.
claims.quote_verbatim: that's basically what all sensors do

claims.claim_text: Filtering has largely moved inside integrated parts, so a converter contains substantial filtering that the buyer never specified and does not need to know about, which is why a digital filter block is not sold as a replacement for an analogue one — it serves a different role in completing a function the customer wanted.
claims.quote_verbatim: the filtering has gone inside chips in such a way that customers don't need to know it's there anymore

claims.claim_text: Any sensor or transducer must be normalised against a standard to mean anything, which is the function calibration laboratories perform across pressure, temperature and the other engineering parameters.
claims.quote_verbatim: anytime you have a sensor, you need to have, or transducer, as it really is, you need to be able to normalize it against a standard
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The range of quantities that can be measured and calibrated against reference standards extends far beyond electrical ones, including flatness and material hardness.
claims.quote_verbatim: they'll have tables for calibrating hardness
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: In a control system the design of the control law is roughly a tenth of the work; the remainder is making the hardware function, interfacing the sensors to the controller and keeping the actuators out of saturation.
claims.quote_verbatim: the actual control system design, actual application of control systems theory
claims.speaker: Kent Lundberg
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Dr. Kent Lundberg - Luculent Linear Legacy

claims.claim_text: A capable control engineer is therefore willing to be an integration engineer, accepting that half the effort on a six-component system goes into connecting those components to one another.
claims.quote_verbatim: half of my time is going to be spent in interfacing these six components together
claims.speaker: Kent Lundberg
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Dr. Kent Lundberg - Luculent Linear Legacy

claims.claim_text: An instrumentation amplifier in its classical form is three operational amplifiers — two taking the inputs, a resistive network between them and a third combining the result — and extracts a small differential signal riding on a large common-mode voltage, which is what makes it suited to electrodes placed on the body.
claims.quote_verbatim: it can read really small signals on top of really large signals, like large common mode stuff
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: AD620, DesignSpark, Instrumentation Amplifier - The Rant Rhetorical

claims.claim_text: Radar's distinguishing properties as a sensing method are that it works through all weather, gives range in three dimensions, and characterises a target by its Doppler signature, which is why it is worth considering alongside infrared, lidar and acoustic options rather than being treated as a specialism.
claims.quote_verbatim: that can see through all weather, that can provide range in three dimensions, that can characterize targets through Doppler signature
claims.speaker: Greg Charvat
claims.episode_title: Greg Charvat Returns With A Book! - Laboratory Literature Laureate

claims.claim_text: Sensing methods should be chosen at the level of the problem being solved rather than by familiarity, with radar treated as a live option when a task calls for a sensor.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you're trying to solve a problem at the highest level and you need a sensor to do a certain task
claims.speaker: Greg Charvat
claims.episode_title: Greg Charvat Returns With A Book! - Laboratory Literature Laureate

claims.claim_text: On a deployed remote sensor the power budget is the overriding design constraint, with sealed battery-powered units expected to last five years without service; on one such programme the transducer itself was the harder technical problem while power consumption was well understood.
claims.quote_verbatim: they have their own batteries, and they have to last for five years
claims.speaker: Greg Charvat
claims.episode_title: Greg Charvat Returns With A Book! - Laboratory Literature Laureate

claims.claim_text: Chemical gas sensors of the common resistive type contain an internal heating element and can require warm-up times measured in tens of minutes, which rules them out of battery-powered applications and drives work to convert older sensing methods to lower-power equivalents.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's a heater elements inside those sensors. So it's not great for low power.
claims.speaker: Richard Ginus

claims.claim_text: Energy harvesting can supply enough power for a low-power microcontroller and a sensor on a continuous basis, including from unconventional sources such as a potential difference developed between two spikes driven into a tree.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's enough to power a little flea-powered microcontroller and a sensor
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: In an automotive electrical system the current is consumed by the sensors, actuators and relays rather than by the processors, and a mechanical relay retains the advantage of drawing no current at all in one of its states.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's not the processors that's sucking down on the current. It's all these, you're dealing with a bunch of sensors and actuators and relays.
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Tom LeMense - Cacaesthestic Chronometric Carriwitchet

claims.claim_text: Resistance temperature detectors small enough to sit directly on an integrated circuit allow the thermal path and dissipation of a board to be instrumented on several channels at once during development.
claims.quote_verbatim: small RTDs that you can place right on ICs on your board and understand heat sources and sinks

claims.claim_text: Integrated circuits intended for radiation environments carry internal sensors monitoring bias, voltage and current conditions, so that a dedicated on-chip processor can detect when a parameter has drifted outside its expected range and run a calibration routine to bring the circuit back into specification.
claims.quote_verbatim: we have a lot of sensors that we put inside the SOCs to monitor bias conditions, voltage conditions, current conditions
claims.speaker: Adrian Tang

claims.claim_text: That approach depends on knowing in advance where every parameter should sit, so the internal measurements are compared against known-good values rather than interpreted; extreme temperature swings are handled by the same calibration mechanism.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's lots of sensors, and you already know where all the parameters should be
claims.speaker: Adrian Tang

claims.claim_text: A shared two-wire bus allows a dozen sensors to be attached using only two pins, which solves the pin-count problem on a constrained module though the component cost accumulates quickly; an addressable expander extends the same trick to general input and output.
claims.quote_verbatim: I can plunk down 12 sensors and only use two pins
claims.speaker: Brandon Harris
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Brandon Harris - Impish Internet Iamatology

claims.claim_text: The kernel subsystem that now carries almost every category of sensor driver originated with a converter manufacturer wanting its own parts well supported, and has since become the place a driver is contributed when a new device appears in a phone or other product.
claims.quote_verbatim: almost every single type of sensor has been pushed into the IIO
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jason Kridner and Robert Nelson

claims.claim_text: Whether to write a sensor driver or adopt an existing one is decided by the reliability required of the production system and by auditing the candidate code, rather than by preference.
claims.quote_verbatim: it depends on the reliability and the quality of any existing driver
claims.speaker: Phillip Johnston
claims.episode_title: Firmware for Hardware Engineers with Phillip Johnston

claims.claim_text: A real-time operating system with a built-in shell exposes sensor and converter readings as interactive commands over a serial connection, so a device can be interrogated for arbitrary readings without writing application code.
claims.quote_verbatim: There's a sensor shell. You can just arbitrarily take sensor readings.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Implementing serial ports in software consumes processor time that scales with the number of ports, whereas a programmable logic device can give each sensor its own dedicated hardware port that polls it and deposits the reading in a register, removing the periodic work from the main program entirely.
claims.quote_verbatim: the more of these software serial ports that you add up, the less CPU time that you have for your actual task at hand
claims.speaker: Luke Valenty

claims.claim_text: Building the peripheral set to match the design, rather than selecting a processor whose fixed peripherals nearly fit, is the argument for putting a soft microcontroller on programmable logic, and modern tooling allows it without writing hardware description code.
claims.quote_verbatim: being able to put together exactly the peripherals that you want
claims.speaker: Luke Valenty

claims.claim_text: Optical sensors demand timing tight enough that programmable logic suits them better than a microcontroller running an operating system, which would have to be substantially more capable to keep up.
claims.quote_verbatim: the sensors require really tight timing
claims.speaker: Leigh Brady

claims.claim_text: The emerging requirement in vision and industrial sensing is low-latency processing placed next to the sensor rather than a bridge device that merely moves data, which is what drives demand for logic capacity in very small, low-power packages.
claims.quote_verbatim: they want to do some low latency computing processing near the sensor
claims.speaker: Sammy Cheung

claims.claim_text: A wireless sensor node can be built to transmit without receiving at all — waking, sending its reading and returning to sleep with no acknowledgement — which is acceptable for quantities such as temperature and humidity where losing occasional samples does not matter.
claims.quote_verbatim: if I miss a sample or two or, or even 10, it's not the end of the world
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Luke Beno of Analog.io

claims.claim_text: The protocol for such a node has to be simple enough to run in a couple of kilobytes of code without a large software library, because the economics require the device to cost a few dollars and to be viable at hundreds of units rather than hundreds of thousands.
claims.quote_verbatim: it should run on, you know, a couple K of code on these embedded devices so that they can cost $3
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Luke Beno of Analog.io

claims.claim_text: Data processing should be kept off the sensor node and moved to where computing is effectively free, reducing the node's job to acquiring and forwarding the reading, which keeps the firmware simple even when the analysis is complex.
claims.quote_verbatim: plug the sensor in, but don't do the data, a lot of data processing there
claims.speaker: Eli Hughes

claims.claim_text: What a customer wants from an instrumented process is information rather than sensor readings, so presenting a dashboard of raw channels misses the point of the deployment.
claims.quote_verbatim: no one cares about like the sensor. They want to know like information.
claims.speaker: Eli Hughes

claims.claim_text: Many industrial problems appear as trends over days or weeks rather than as sudden failures, which is what makes continuous monitoring valuable enough to justify instrumenting an expensive machine.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's, it's over days or weeks that you notice a trend.
claims.speaker: Eli Hughes

claims.claim_text: Machine learning applied to sensor output replaces hand characterisation: instead of deciding that a particular slope means a particular event, examples of the event are recorded many times and the classifier is trained on them, which removes the need to derive thresholds or signal-processing rules by hand.
claims.quote_verbatim: You close the door and you do that a hundred times and you collect this data.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The alternative that most practitioners actually implement is a threshold comparison, which is why an automatically characterised classifier is attractive to engineers without signal-processing expertise.
claims.quote_verbatim: basically all I can do is like threshold
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A deployed sensor whose readings have consequences for the operator will be tampered with, so the design has to anticipate the unit being disabled, a different sensor being substituted, or a reading being spoofed, and answer it with authentication that the attached hardware is genuine.
claims.quote_verbatim: such as, like, disabling the sensor or even swapping out to a different sensor
claims.speaker: Akiba

claims.claim_text: Tyre pressure monitoring is a widely deployed radio sensor system in which four independent transmitters periodically send to a central controller, radio being the only practical way to get data off a rotating wheel.
claims.quote_verbatim: you've got four sensors, one in each tire, and each one is independently transmitting periodically a radio signal
claims.speaker: Michael Ossmann
claims.episode_title: A Security Update with Michael Ossmann

claims.claim_text: Because such a sensor carries its own processor and reports onto the vehicle's internal bus, a substituted or modified one is a route onto that bus from outside the vehicle.
claims.quote_verbatim: the flat tyre sensor has a micro in it, you know, and it hooks onto the bus and it reports back
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: A Security Update with Michael Ossmann

claims.claim_text: Attacking the analogue-to-digital conversion stage rather than a specific device defeats a whole class of sensors at once, since so many share that conversion step.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you figure out how to defeat an analog to digital converter, then you figured out how to defeat a huge range of sensors
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Not every sensor presents a digital output, so an analysis that assumes a digital interface does not cover the field.
claims.quote_verbatim: not all sensors are digital output
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Placing the sensing element on a daughter board rather than the main board allows it to be revised repeatedly while better parts are being evaluated, without respinning the whole design each time.
claims.quote_verbatim: The IMU was on a daughter board so I could re-spin the board more often
claims.speaker: Piotr Esden-Tempski

claims.claim_text: A forced sensor substitution has a larger consequence than a comparable power-supply substitution, because different sensing parts branch the firmware and leave separate builds to be maintained against each board revision.
claims.quote_verbatim: if there's like a sensor difference now you're, you just branched your firm, your firmware
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Mixed Signal Education with Philip Salmony

claims.claim_text: Standardised sensor connector families exist precisely so that a researcher can attach a measurement without designing an interface, and a board can carry several of them at once to cover the common ecosystems.
claims.quote_verbatim: I put on basically every sensor interface I could find
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The people specifying sensing systems are frequently not electronic engineers at all — mechanical, civil and materials specialists fill the training courses — because what they want is the data and the process improvement, with the electronics incidental.
claims.quote_verbatim: most people don't give a crap about electronics. They care about data
claims.speaker: Scott Miller

claims.claim_text: A company with a physical process and high volume but no hardware capability is a recognisable customer type for sensing products, since the problem is worth solving at their scale but standing up a hardware team is not something they want to do.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's like a startup that just doesn't have a lot of experience in hardware, but they do have the ability to move like really high volume
claims.speaker: Scott Miller

claims.claim_text: Mechanical engineers reach electronics through measurement: needing stress or temperature data leads to attaching a sensor, which has to be powered, which leads to recording the data.
claims.quote_verbatim: you're concerned about stress or temperature or whatever it is in your parts. Well, how do you get that information? Well, you put a sensor on
claims.speaker: Ryan O'Hara
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ryan O'Hara - Keyed, Kerfed Kapton

claims.claim_text: When following a tutorial, substituting a different vendor's sensor for the one specified is a common cause of failure that is very hard to diagnose, because the difference is hidden under layers of abstraction; duplicating the exact hardware is the reliable way to reach a working baseline.
claims.quote_verbatim: the only way I was eventually able to get it to work is by exactly duplicating everything that someone else had done
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The value of a kit in learning is that every copy is identical, which removes the variable that makes a substituted part so difficult to debug.
claims.quote_verbatim: the important thing about kits is the fact that they're all the same
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Sensors themselves are approachable, with the difficulty appearing only once estimation techniques such as filtering and orientation mathematics are required.
claims.quote_verbatim: Once you get to Kelman's and Quaternian's, it gets a little more difficult, but just the sensors
claims.speaker: Elecia White

claims.claim_text: In a stabilised flying platform the sensors report attitude and motion, but the engineering difficulty is in the control loop that consumes those inputs and recovers the vehicle from a disturbance.
claims.quote_verbatim: taking all that input, cranking on it, and then actually reacting to it
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Products of that kind emerge from a confluence rather than a single advance: low-cost sensors arriving alongside cheaper processing, motors and batteries is what made small autonomous aircraft practical.
claims.quote_verbatim: the confluence of low-cost sensors and increasing power and lower costs on just all components and the motors available and the batteries
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A capability that once represented years of work by a design team is now bought as a module with a standard header and attached to a product directly.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's buy a person sensor. And stick it on your product. It's got a quick header on it.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Deployed sensing systems fail through mundane physical causes rather than exotic ones — a connection knocked out, a power cut with no clean restart, a flat battery, or the unit physically disturbed — which is what any claim of a maintenance-free installation has to answer.
claims.quote_verbatim: The batteries run out on the, the little, the little sensor thingy.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Vehicles now carry a processor and sensing in each subsystem down to the level of a door handle, because the function requires local detection.
claims.quote_verbatim: the door handle needs its own micro, you know, because it needs to detect that
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A general-purpose sensing platform is best built by keeping the node generic and swapping the attached sensor, rather than by building a distinct product for each measurement.
claims.quote_verbatim: can you zoom back and just swap out what sensors in there
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Bridging an unfamiliar sensor to a host computer through a small microcontroller and a serial terminal is the standard first step in evaluating it, and the repeated need for that bridge is what such general-purpose interface tools are built to serve.
claims.quote_verbatim: write some basic firmware that can just bridge that sensor to a UART terminal
claims.speaker: Jonathan Georgino

claims.claim_text: Power profiling of a sensing device proceeds by removing one contributor at a time — substituting a fabricated message for a real sensor reading, for example — to establish how much each part of the system consumes, since optimising a small contributor while a large one dominates yields nothing.
claims.quote_verbatim: instead of turning on the sensor, you just make up a message, right? So now you know how much your sensor contributed.

claims.claim_text: Very low-power remote sensors relaying through satellites allow instrumentation of assets in places with no other connectivity, such as fields, water tanks and livestock.
claims.quote_verbatim: very low-power remote sensors that you can put out in fields or on cattle or on water tanks
claims.speaker: Dan Esparon
claims.episode_title: Satellite Design Engineering with Dan Esparon
